newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt prices mixed, eye Fujimori comments.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt prices mixed, eye Fujimori comments.

text.p: Emerging debt prices were mixed to higher in relatively active trade on Monday, bolstered mostly by solid bidding in Latin American Brady debt, market experts said.
"The market is better bid overall and we are still seeing better demand," said a trader at a large U.S. investment bank.

In Latin American debt, market participants received Peru President Alberto Fujimori's annual State of the Nation address with a moderately positive response. Peruvian Brady paper rallied in late morning ahead of the Peruvian leader's speech and ended tighter on the day, traders said.

Fujimori, who has been mired in political turmoil and exceedingly low public approval ratings, reiterated some soothing words to the investment community about the fiscal state of his nation's economy.

Fujimori said the government had bought back $3.4 billion of the country's debt, which was slightly higher than many analysts' expectations. He also said Peru's net international reserves were at $10 billion for the first time in the country's history.
Richard Segal, head of fixed-income research at Santander Investments, said Fujimori's confirmation of an actual debt buyback figure is a positive step toward a more transparent government.
"The fact that (Fujimori) has been trasparent about how much the government has bought back is quite refreshing," he said.

Fujimori offered some relief to public-sector workers, increasing their wages 15 percent starting in August. Segal said the wage increase may raise a few eyebrows about inflation, but should not spur major inflationary pressures.
"On the whole, it shouldn't be too harmful to the inflation outlook -- as long as they don't expect 15 percent next year, too," he said.
Peru PDI bonds rose 7/8 point to 65-3/4 bid and FLIRBS gained 5/8 point to 59-7/8 bid.
In other Latin Brady debt, Argentine Par bonds were about 10 basis points tighter on the day, said one trader.
Argentine Pars were up 3/4 at 74-7/8 bid.
Meanwhile, Brazilian "C" bonds were up 7/8 at 83-5/8 bid, while Mexican Pars edged up 3/8 to 81-3/4 bid.
In Eastern European debt, Russian Vnesh loans traded heavily on Monday, one trader said.
Dollar-denominated Vnesh loans were down about 3/4 of a point when New York opened this morning and recovered about half that later in the day, he said.
Dollar Vnesh were off 1/4 at 94 bid in late trading.
